title: Controlled neck surgery
mathematical_role: Represent the local S² × I neck model, two cutting spheres, excision, cap attachment, and topology bookkeeping as distinct stages.
learning_objective: Distinguish a three-dimensional neck cross-section from a planar cut metaphor and understand that surgery changes topology under imported geometric control.
literal_semantics: The teaching sequence is identify neck → cut/remove → attach cap models.
Two separate dashed cross-sections are explicitly labelled S²₋ and S²₊.
The local neck type is explicitly labelled S² × I.
Topology bookkeeping is explicitly separated from the geometric reconstruction.
nonliteral_semantics: The rendered tube is a perspective schematic, not a literal metric three-manifold.
The cut ellipses are pictorial projections of two-sphere cross-sections, not computed embeddings.
The cap shapes are standard-cap teaching models, not numerically constructed surgery caps.
No displayed length or radius is a canonical-neighbourhood or surgery scale.

notes: Canonical-neighbourhood and surgery-scale validity remain imported theorem context and are not inferred from the drawing.

renderer.version_or_environment: Python 3 standard library; deterministic SVG renderer v1
reproducibility_notes: No randomness or external service is used.
Run the generator from any checkout; output paths and bytes are deterministic under the recorded Python-standard-library contract.

derivatives.role: annotated vector master and static web review candidate

accessibility.alt_text: A three-stage schematic of an S2 by I neck: identify the neck, cut along two labelled sphere cross-sections and remove the middle, then attach standard-cap models.
accessibility.long_description: Three panels show a perspective tube with a narrow central neck, then two dashed sphere cross-sections labelled S2 minus and S2 plus with the middle excised, then two capped components. A topology-bookkeeping box states that cutting changes topology and must be recorded and later reversed. A boundary states that the plate does not certify a valid surgery event.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: Pedagogical reconstruction of the identify-cut-remove-cap sequence and its topology-bookkeeping obligation.
not_claimed: Validity of a specific surgery event
A Ricci-flow construction or proof of the Poincare theorem

supersession_reason: The successor replaces the planar dumbbell metaphor with an explicitly three-dimensional neck reconstruction and separate S² cutting surfaces.
